guideline: Annotators classified errors in generated actions into three types: Object Localization and Inference errors, Object Affordance errors, and Insufficient Interaction Coverage errors.
Annotators identified three error categories: Object Localization and Inference (OLI) errors, Object Affordance errors, and Insufficient Interaction Coverage errors.

We define these as reasoning errors wherein the model fails to track the current location of object(s), i.e. whether an object is found in the inventory, the surrounding environment, or is not found at all. These errors occur when an incorrect understanding of the affordance of objects leads the model to generate actions which are nonsensical or impossible. We define these errors as those in which, despite the presence of objects, the model's generation is insufficient to enumerate all possible interactions with the objects.
